While the story is well-written, atmospheric, and offers a quiet, grounded slice-of-life portrayal of a ferrywoman's morning routine in Northern Germany, it relies on very familiar literary tropes (stoic rural characters, the timelessness of nature, the contrast between traditional manual work and modern technology like the vibrating phone). Because the story has no real resolution or exploration of a novel theme—leaving the plot threads like the phone call completely unexplained—an average reader will appreciate the mood and character sketch, but will not walk away with a unique or original idea that challenges beliefs or provides new insights.
